basis: Idiopathic noninfectious uveitis is immune-mediated inflammation involving the uvea, retina and vitreous.
Inflammatory occlusive vasculitis; ischemic sensory neuropathy and skin ulceration/gangrene each reported in 80-99%.
Malignant T-cell lymphoma; extranodal sites vary without a consistently affected additional organ.
Defined by myocardial hypertrophy and associated cardiac dysfunction.
Polyp arising in the large intestine.
Malignant hematopoietic dendritic-cell neoplasm; skin infiltration occurs in roughly 30-50% of reported cases.
Cholesterol emboli obstruct renal vessels and directly injure the kidney.
Phosphate deficiency causes defective bone mineralization; renal phosphate-reabsorption dysfunction underlies most cases, although nutritional forms occur.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder defined by brain malformations, microcephaly, epilepsy and central spasticity.
Inherited bile phospholipid transport disorder causing intrahepatic cholestasis during pregnancy; pruritus does not establish skin damage.
Inherited ocular refractive disorder; high myopia in 8/8 patients.
Inherited platelet adhesion dysfunction causing bleeding; bruising does not establish a separate skin disorder.
Inherited LDL metabolism disorder; premature atherosclerosis is very common but separately diagnosed vascular disease. Hepatic steatosis is also separately coded.
Maternal ABO antibodies cause neonatal red-cell hemolysis and unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; jaundice alone does not indicate liver damage.
Brain injury causes dyskinetic motor dysfunction; impaired eating and limb movements do not establish direct gastrointestinal or muscle damage.
Mechanical inward turning of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Inherited ventricular myocardial disease causing arrhythmia and predominantly right ventricular dysfunction.
Hereditary fibrous overgrowth of the gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Systemic venular dysfunction supported by cardiovascular abnormalities and cyanosis; no evidence of another directly damaged organ.
Microcephaly with cognitive impairment; endocrine dysfunction includes low free T4 in 2/5, elevated TSH in 3/5 and autoimmune hypoparathyroidism in 2/2.
Pterygia, limb malformations and oral clefts define the syndrome; microphthalmia, corneal opacity and ankyloblepharon in the sole reported patient (1/1).
Amino acid transport disorder with intellectual disability and progressive tremor; urinary duplication lacks demonstrated dysfunction; hypothyroidism is occasional.
Treponema infection directly inflames the meninges.
Isolated congenital impairment of brain growth; no additional organ involvement defines this umbrella concept.
Cerebellopontine angle nerve-sheath tumor, usually vestibular schwannoma; direct auditory nerve dysfunction causes hearing loss in over 70%.
